names.official: Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA)

taxes.base: Supplies of goods and services by businesses in France and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and deduct input VAT.

rate.headline: 20% standard; 10%, 5.5% and 2.1% reduced
details: 5.5% on most food, books, energy subscriptions and some housing works; 10% on restaurants, passenger transport, renovation and accommodation; 2.1% on reimbursed medicines and some press.

instruments.explanation: The largest tax by revenue after the social contributions. The State collects it and assigns a growing share of the yield to social security and to the local governments (which replaced their abolished taxes with VAT shares); that assigned share is counted here, once.
exceptions: Financial, medical, educational and insurance services are exempt.

names.official: Impôt sur le revenu des personnes physiques (IRPP)

taxes.base: Household income (wages, pensions, business, rental and capital income) divided by the number of family "parts" (family quotient).
taxes.payer: Households; withheld at source on wages and pensions since 2019.

details: Five bands applied to income per part of the household; the benefit of the family quotient is capped per half-part.
Capital income is mostly taxed separately under the flat tax (PFU): 12.8% income tax plus social levies.
A differential contribution of at least 20% on very high incomes applies from 2025 (about EUR 0.4 billion).

instruments.explanation: Only about half of French households pay it; the larger income-based take is the CSG. Revenue here is net of the tax credits (EUR 9.3 billion in 2025).
exceptions: Many tax credits and reductions for childcare, home help, donations and others.

names.official: Impôt sur les sociétés (IS) et contribution sociale sur les bénéfices

taxes.base: Profits of companies and other legal entities.

rate.headline: 25%; 15% on the first EUR 42,500 for small firms
details: 25% since 2022; 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of profit for qualifying small companies; a 3.3% social surcharge on the part above EUR 763,000. In 2025 an exceptional surcharge applied to the largest companies.

instruments.explanation: Revenue is net of tax credits (EUR 10.1 billion in 2025, among them the research credit).

names.official: Contribution sociale généralisée (CSG)

taxes.base: Employment income, replacement income, pensions, capital and gaming income, on a broad base set apart from income tax.

rate.headline: 9.2% on wages; lower on pensions; 10.6% on most capital income
details: 9.2% of 98.25% of gross salary (6.8 points deductible from income tax); 8.3%, 6.6% or 3.8% on pensions depending on income; 10.6% on most capital income from 2026 (9.2% before; life insurance stays at 9.2%), which brings total social levies on it to 18.6%.

instruments.explanation: A tax earmarked for the social security system and the second-largest charge in the country. INSEE counts it as an income tax, not as a contribution, because it carries no entitlement.

names.official: Contribution au remboursement de la dette sociale (CRDS)

taxes.base: The same wide base as the CSG.

details: Created in 1996 to pay off the social security debt; the end date has been extended to 2033.

instruments.explanation: A small flat levy that pays off the accumulated social security deficit.

names.official: Prélèvements sur les revenus du capital (prélèvement de solidarité et prélèvement forfaitaire sur les revenus de capitaux mobiliers)

taxes.base: Interest, dividends and gains of households, withheld at source.

rate.headline: Flat tax of 31.4% (12.8% income tax + 18.6% social levies)
details: The flat tax rose from 30% to 31.4% in 2026 because the CSG on most capital income went from 9.2% to 10.6% (life insurance stays at 30%). The solidarity levy of 7.5% is one of the social levies; the withholding on investment income is the income-tax part.

instruments.explanation: Grouped here: the solidarity levy and other social contributions on capital income (EUR 14.4 billion) and the withholding on movable capital income (EUR 5.3 billion).
exceptions: Savings schemes such as the Livret A and the PEL are exempt or taxed differently.

names.official: Cotisations sociales effectives (employeurs et salariés)

taxes.base: Gross wages (with reduced employer rates near the minimum wage), and the earnings of the self-employed.
taxes.payer: Employers (the larger share), employees and the self-employed.

rate.headline: Several rates by scheme and by wage band
details: Contributions pay for health, pensions (basic and the Agirc-Arrco complementary scheme), family benefits, unemployment insurance and work accidents; employer contributions are cut for wages up to 3.5 times the minimum wage.

instruments.explanation: The biggest single flow: about a third of all compulsory levies. INSEE counts only the effective contributions; imputed contributions (EUR 52.4 billion), such as the State’s pension costs for its own employees, are left out.

names.official: Taxe intérieure de consommation sur les produits énergétiques (TICPE)

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel, heating oil and other petroleum products by the litre.
taxes.payer: Fuel suppliers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: A fixed amount per litre by fuel; regions may add a regional rate
details: Rates differ by product (petrol, diesel, heating oil); part of the yield goes to the regions and départements.

instruments.explanation: The largest excise duty. The State shares part of it with the regions and départements.
exceptions: Reduced rates for farmers, fishers, taxis and some transport.

legalRefs.locator: Code des douanes, arts. 265 and following

names.official: Accises sur l’électricité (TICFE), le gaz naturel (TICGN) et autres taxes sur l’énergie
names.common: Excise on electricity, gas and other energy

taxes.base: Electricity and natural gas supplied to consumers, and other energy products.

rate.headline: Per megawatt hour
details: The electricity tax was raised back to its normal level in 2025 after being cut to the minimum during the energy crisis.

instruments.explanation: Revenue from the electricity tax nearly doubled in 2025 (EUR 4.8 billion to 8.3 billion).

names.official: Accises sur les tabacs (droits de consommation)

taxes.base: Cigarettes and other tobacco products.
taxes.payer: Manufacturers and distributors; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Share of the retail price plus a minimum per 1,000
details: An ad valorem rate on the retail price with a minimum tax per thousand cigarettes.

instruments.explanation: The retail price of tobacco is set by the manufacturers and approved by the State.

names.official: Accises sur les alcools et boissons

taxes.base: Spirits, wine, beer and some other beverages.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

instruments.explanation: Includes the duty on sugary drinks.

names.official: Droits de mutation à titre gratuit (successions et donations)

taxes.base: The value of what is inherited or given, above allowances that depend on the relationship.

rate.headline: 5%–45% for close relatives; up to 60% for non-relatives
details: A EUR 100,000 allowance for each child, renewable every 15 years for gifts; spouses and civil partners are exempt on inheritance.

instruments.explanation: EUR 16.1 billion on inheritances and EUR 5.0 billion on gifts in 2025.

names.official: Impôt sur la fortune immobilière (IFI)

taxes.base: Net real-estate assets of a household above EUR 1.3 million.

details: The general wealth tax (ISF) was replaced by this tax on real estate only in 2018.

instruments.explanation: The remaining form of annual wealth tax.

names.official: Taxe sur les conventions d’assurances, taxe de solidarité additionnelle et autres taxes sur les contrats d’assurance

taxes.base: Premiums of most insurance contracts, including supplementary health insurance.

rate.headline: Rates vary by type of contract
details: Proceeds go partly to the départements and to health and social funds.

instruments.explanation: Includes the additional solidarity tax on supplementary health insurance (EUR 6.6 billion).

names.official: Prélèvements sur les jeux, casinos, paris sportifs et hippiques

taxes.base: The gross gaming revenue of the national lottery, casinos and betting operators.

instruments.explanation: Includes the CSG and CRDS levied on gaming.

names.official: Taxe sur les salaires

taxes.base: Wages paid by employers that are not subject to VAT (banks, insurers, associations, hospitals).

instruments.explanation: A payroll tax that replaces VAT cost recovery for activities exempt from VAT.

names.official: Contributions pour la formation professionnelle et l’apprentissage

taxes.base: Employers’ total payroll.

rate.headline: About 1% of payroll
details: 0.55% or 1% of payroll for vocational training plus the apprenticeship tax of 0.68%.

instruments.explanation: Collected by the social security collectors and passed to the training funds.

names.official: Forfait social et autres contributions patronales (FNAL, CNSA, PEEC, AGS, stock-options)
names.common: Social surcharge and other employer levies

taxes.base: Profit-sharing and supplementary pension payments (forfait social), and employers’ payroll for the housing, autonomy, construction and wage-guarantee funds.

rate.headline: Forfait social 20%; others as a share of payroll
details: Forfait social EUR 6.6 billion, FNAL EUR 3.0 billion, CNSA EUR 2.5 billion, AGS EUR 1.7 billion, PEEC EUR 1.5 billion and the employer levy on stock options EUR 1.5 billion.

instruments.explanation: A group of earmarked employer levies reported separately by INSEE.

names.official: Contribution sociale de solidarité des sociétés (C3S)

taxes.base: Turnover of companies above EUR 19 million.

rate.headline: 0.16% of turnover
details: A turnover-based levy that funds the self-employed workers’ pension scheme; it is being phased out for smaller firms.

instruments.explanation: A tax on turnover rather than profit.

instruments.statusNote: The tax is being phased out by law; the rate falls each year until it is abolished.

names.official: Cotisation sur la valeur ajoutée des entreprises (CVAE)

taxes.base: The value added of businesses with turnover above EUR 500,000.

rate.headline: A declining rate, being phased out
details: The tax is being abolished in stages; its revenue now goes to the State and local governments receive VAT shares in compensation.

instruments.explanation: A tax that was once the main local business tax.

names.official: Droits d’importation au profit de l’Union européenne

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU.

instruments.explanation: Collected by French customs; INSEE records them as an EU tax.

names.official: Taxe sur les transactions financières

taxes.base: Purchases of shares of French companies with a market value above EUR 1 billion, and high-frequency and some derivative trades.

rate.headline: 0.4% of the purchase price (from 2025)
details: The rate doubled from 0.3% to 0.4% in 2025.

instruments.explanation: Revenue rose from EUR 1.9 billion to EUR 2.6 billion.

names.official: Taxes environnementales (TGAP, redevances des agences de l’eau, quotas carbone, contributions des producteurs d’électricité)

taxes.base: Pollution, water use, carbon emissions and electricity production.

rate.headline: A different rate for each
details: TGAP EUR 1.1 billion, water agency charges EUR 2.2 billion, carbon quotas EUR 1.5 billion and electricity producers’ contributions EUR 0.7 billion.

instruments.explanation: A group of environmental charges reported separately by INSEE.

names.official: Autres taxes sur les entreprises (IFER, taxes consulaires, taxes sur les véhicules et les bureaux)

taxes.base: Network operators’ flat-rate charges (IFER), chambers of commerce, company vehicles and offices.

rate.headline: A different rate for each
details: IFER EUR 2.3 billion, consular taxes EUR 1.3 billion, company vehicle taxes EUR 1.2 billion, office taxes EUR 1.0 billion.

instruments.explanation: A group of smaller taxes on businesses.

names.official: Autres impôts de l’État (droits d’enregistrement hors DMTO, malus automobile, taxes sur les transports, le numérique, les spectacles, les ventes de produits pharmaceutiques)

taxes.base: Registration duties other than on property sales, the car penalty (malus), transport, digital and entertainment taxes and a levy on pharmaceutical sales.

rate.headline: A different rate for each
details: Registration duties 2.5, transport services 2.5, digital and telecom 1.1, malus 0.9, entertainment 0.8 and pharmaceutical sales 0.8 (EUR billion).

instruments.explanation: The remainder of the State’s taxes, each below about 0.2% of the national total.

names.official: Droits de mutation à titre onéreux (DMTO)

taxes.base: The price of second-hand homes and other property sold.

rate.headline: About 6% of the price
details: The départements’ rate may be raised from 4.5% to 5% from 2025 for three years; with the communal part the total is about 5.8% to 6.4%.

instruments.explanation: The largest tax that the départements control. It is volatile with the housing market: EUR 14.7 billion in 2024 and EUR 17.7 billion in 2025.
exceptions: New homes pay a reduced rate.

names.official: Taxe sur les certificats d’immatriculation des véhicules

taxes.base: The registration of a vehicle, by horsepower and emissions.

rate.headline: EUR per fiscal horsepower, set by each region
details: Each region sets the price per fiscal horsepower.

instruments.explanation: The whole yield belongs to the regions.
exceptions: Electric vehicles are often exempt or reduced by the region.

names.official: Octroi de mer (départements et régions d’outre-mer)

taxes.base: Goods imported or produced in the overseas departments.

instruments.explanation: A levy of the overseas collectivities, with a part classified by INSEE as a tax on imports.

names.official: Taxe foncière sur les propriétés bâties et non bâties

taxes.base: The cadastral rental value of buildings and land.
taxes.payer: The owner (paid by households and businesses).

rate.headline: Rates voted by each commune and group of communes
details: Since 2021 the départements’ share has been transferred to the communes, which now receive the whole tax; the cadastral values were last revised in the 1970s and are indexed each year.

instruments.explanation: The main local tax and the largest tax controlled by local governments: EUR 27.0 billion paid by households and EUR 17.2 billion by businesses.
exceptions: New buildings are exempt for two years; low-income elderly owners may be exempt.

names.official: Cotisation foncière des entreprises (CFE)

taxes.base: The rental value of the premises used by a business.

instruments.explanation: The part of the old business tax (taxe professionnelle) that remains local.

names.official: Versement mobilité (versement transport)

taxes.base: Payroll of employers with at least 11 employees in a transport authority’s area.

rate.headline: Up to about 3% of payroll, set by the transport authority
details: The ceiling depends on the area: highest in the Paris region and the biggest cities.

instruments.explanation: A payroll tax earmarked for local public transport.

names.official: Taxe d’habitation sur les résidences secondaires et autres locaux meublés

taxes.base: Second homes and other non-primary residences.

rate.headline: Rate voted by the commune
details: The tax on main residences was abolished for all households by 2023; only second homes remain.

instruments.explanation: What is left of the housing tax.

names.official: Autres taxes locales (taxe de séjour, GEMAPI, TASCOM, taxes additionnelles aux impôts fonciers)

taxes.base: Overnight stays, flood and water-body management, large retail surfaces and levies added to the property taxes.
taxes.payer: Tourists, property owners and large retailers.

rate.headline: Set locally
details: Tourist tax EUR 1.3 billion, retail surfaces EUR 1.2 billion, GEMAPI EUR 0.6 billion and levies attached to the property tax EUR 0.8 billion.

instruments.explanation: The smaller local taxes reported by INSEE.
